Subject: Post-call onramp: SDK local runbook, auth & routing next steps

Thanks again for the time today — good initial discovery. Below is a concise runbook that captures the technical asks and the recommended minimal path to get a working local proof-of-concept (PoC) that demonstrates: auth, routing, structured output (tool calling), and embeddings/reranking. Please review and flag anything missing.

Summary of priorities (from today's call)
- Priority 1: Get a local dev flow with Redwood SDK (Python + TypeScript) and a sample chat app to validate auth and routing.
- Priority 2: Validate embeddings pipeline and a small reranker against a sample dataset.
- Priority 3: Demo structured outputs / tool calling (calendar lookups) using a trivial tool adapter.

Minimum runbook (3 steps)
1) Local environment 
   - Clone the quickstart bundle we attached (redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip).
   - Create a .env using the attached env-vars-example.env (set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION, DEV_ROUTING_PROFILE).
   - Recommended commands:
       - Python: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python examples/chat_server.py
       - TS: cd typescript && yarn && yarn dev --env .env.local

2) Auth & routing smoke test
   - Use a dev API key (we can generate a short-lived key for you) and run the basic generate call. Verify response and headers include x-redwood-route.
   - Routing check: we will seed DEV_ROUTING_PROFILE to prefer low-latency hosted variants for the PoC.

3) Embeddings + reranker
   - Run embeddings job (examples/embeddings_batch.py) with the sample dataset under /data/sample_faqs.jsonl.
   - Run a small reranker demo (typescript/reranker-demo) to validate relevance ordering.

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip (sample apps + docs), env-vars-example.env, lumina-integration-mvp-plan.pdf

Proposed next steps / timeline
- Today (within 24h): Redwood provides a 48-hour dev API key + link to quickstart Drive.
- By EOD Tue (48h): Lumina runs the quickstart locally and shares the run log/any failing commands.
- Follow-up sync: 30-min technical checkpoint after your initial run (schedule via Calendly link below).

Ask list for Lumina (please reply inline):
- Confirm which dev machine you will use (mac/linux, GPU/no-GPU).
- Any network policy that would block outbound to redwood endpoints?
- Are you okay with short-lived API keys for the local PoC?

Calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/sdks-30m
Drive quickstart: https://drive.redwood.example.com/link/sdks/quickstart

Thanks — I’ll generate the dev key once you confirm machine/os and we’ll push the attachments to the shared Drive as well.

—

Thanks Alex — perfect. For the PoC we strongly recommend starting with an in-memory vector store (faiss/simple numpy) to keep complexity low. If the in-memory path is successful, we can switch to a managed connector in the next sprint.

Additional quicknotes and commands (put these in a README in the zip):
- API key usage: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_dev_XXXX
- Region: export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
- Basic generate check (curl):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model": "redwood-mini-1", "input": "hello"}'

- Routing check: the response will include headers like x-redwood-route; a value of "hosted/fast" indicates the dev routing profile is active.

Structured output / tool calling
- examples/tool_adapter/calendar_adapter.py demonstrates a minimal adapter that receives structured JSON from the model and executes a mock calendar lookup.
- We’ll instrument the example to log the tool calls so you can validate the round trip.

Attachments: we attached the quickstart bundle to this thread and uploaded to Drive (link above). I’ll also add a short troubleshooting checklist:
- Common failure: missing env var REDWOOD_API_KEY (quick error).
- Proxy issues: set HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY and add --proxy if yarn/curl fail.

Next: I’ll provision a 48-hour dev key and drop it into the Drive in a protected file. Expect that within 2 hours.

—
Karthik

Quick technical note from eng (adding a couple of gotchas we hit during internal pilots):
- Local dev container: we include docker-compose.dev.yml in the zip. If you use the container, mount ~/.cache to avoid repeated model downloads.
- Tokenization mismatch: if you run the Python embeddings example, pin tokenizers==0.14.1 in the venv to match the runtime we used for the dataset.
- Reranker: the TypeScript reranker-demo uses a tiny re-ranking model (rerank-small). Latency will be fine for 500-row datasets; for larger datasets we recommend batching embeddings creation and using faiss or a managed vector DB.

If you want, we can jump on a 20-min screenshare during your first run and debug any environment issues. Karthik — I can volunteer time Tue morning PST.

Thanks,
